title: Brampton Diwali Mela Returns November 8 With Bhangra, Fireworks and Drones
excerpt: Sukhshinder Shinda headlines the free Sesquicentennial Park celebration from 4 to 10 p.m., with fireworks at 7:30 p.m. and a drone show at 8:15 p.m.
body:
• Brampton's Diwali Mela returns to Sesquicentennial Park, 11333 Bramalea Road, on Sunday, November 8, 2026, from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. — admission is free.
  • Punjabi singer Sukhshinder Shinda headlines the RBC main stage, with Vandana Kaur opening and a cultural programme of Bhangra, Gidda, Kathak, Garba, classical dance and dhol.
  • Fireworks run 7:30-7:45 p.m. and the drone show 8:15-8:27 p.m.; both may be cancelled in high winds.
  • Reader plan: on-site parking is extremely limited — use the free Brampton Transit shuttles every 30 minutes from Mount Pleasant GO Station, Sheridan College, Gore Meadows Community Centre and Brampton Soccer Centre, and leave personal fireworks at home: Brampton bans them, with penalties starting at $500.

Brampton's annual Diwali Mela returns on Sunday, November 8, bringing six hours of live music, cultural performances, food and family activities to Sesquicentennial Park. The City of Brampton's free celebration runs from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. and closes with both a fireworks display and a drone show.

The programme

According to the City of Brampton news release, main stage performances presented by RBC include a headline set by renowned Punjabi singer Sukhshinder Shinda and an opening performance by Vandana Kaur. ToDo Canada's event listing names further performers including Nachdi Jawani, Rajasthanis In Toronto, Joti Dhillon and Poojan Kholi and Band, across a programme of Bhangra, Gidda, Kathak, Garba, classical dance and dhol. Food vendors and activities for all ages run throughout the evening.

The event is supported by Bell, CAA, Primont, Mattamy Homes, TD and Tim Hortons, alongside fireworks sponsor Performance Auto Group.

"I am proud to welcome residents to our fourth annual Diwali Mela, where families and friends can enjoy vibrant performances, share in the joy of the Festival of Lights and celebrate the traditions and community spirit that make Brampton so special."

— Patrick Brown, Mayor, City of Brampton

Fireworks and the drone show

The fireworks display, presented by Performance Auto Group, runs from 7:30 p.m. to 7:45 p.m., followed by the drone show from 8:15 p.m. to 8:27 p.m. Both displays may be cancelled if high winds or unfavourable weather create safety concerns.

Diwali, the Festival of Lights, symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness and is celebrated by Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and Buddhists, the City noted. Traditions include lighting diyas, creating rangolis, exchanging gifts and sharing meals. The festival also coincides with Bandi Chhor Divas, celebrated by Sikhs — a pairing of particular resonance in Brampton, home to one of Canada's largest Sikh communities.

Getting there

Sesquicentennial Park is at 11333 Bramalea Road. On-site parking is extremely limited, so the City encourages visitors to use free Brampton Transit shuttles running every 30 minutes from four locations: Mount Pleasant GO Station, Sheridan College, Gore Meadows Community Centre and Brampton Soccer Centre. Shuttles to the park run from 3:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m., with return service from 4:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. Temporary road closures will also affect parts of Claremont Drive and Countryside Drive between 2 p.m. and 11:55 p.m.

Full details are on the City's Diwali Mela release page.

Celebrate safely

Under Brampton's Fireworks By-law, the use, purchase, discharge, possession, display, sale and offering of fireworks is prohibited, with penalties starting at $500. Sparklers, while permitted under the by-law, are not allowed at the Diwali Mela itself. The City encourages residents to attend the official show instead, and to keep music and noise at a reasonable level under its public nuisance and noise by-laws.

For GTA families weighing their Diwali weekend, Brampton's Mela is the anchor event on the main day itself — free, outdoors, and scheduled so the fireworks and drone show both land before children's bedtimes on a school night.
